newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends off but steady as U.S. trims losses.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends off but steady as U.S. trims losses.

text.p: IPE Brent crude ended weaker but rangebound on Tuesday as steadier U.S. product prices prevented the extension of early losses prompted by sloppy European spot markets, dealers said.
Dec Brent closed at $22.80 a barrel, down 21 cents, but five cents off the session.
Many players were unwilling to take on new positions ahead of the release of U.S. inventory data due to be published after the market closed.
"There has been some paper buying in the U.S. but it's been mainly short-covering - nobody's adding length," said a dealer.
The American Petroleum Institute (API) stocks report for the week ending November 8 is expected to show modest builds in crude and products, according to traders and analysts surveyed by Reuters.

Earlier on Tuesday, the Euroilstock Foundation said middle distillate stocks in the European Union, excluding Sweden, rose 6.60 million barrels in October, trimming the year-on-year shortfall to 21.65 million barrels or 6.9 percent.
The delivery of a record 856,100 tonnes of heating oil into the Rotterdam barge market against the expiring November gas oil contract also knocked European sentiment, dealers said.
European crude spot markets were under pressure from an overhang of late November Brent which could prompt further losses unless an arbitrage to the U.S. opens up, they added.
IPE Dec gas oil closed 75 cents lower at $211.00 per tonne after Nov expired at $220.00 when the prompt backwardation stood at $8.50.
The Dec/Jan spread ended at a more modest $4 premium.
